items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: He said I was the most apt student that he ever had.

ctx.x: be top trombone players. And they didn't know it was going to happen to me.

But he was a very meticulous man. He didn't care who you were. If you were serious about it he would help you. Because after he found out I was serious he told me, look, if you don't have any money come out anyway and take your lesson. Because -- and he paid me a high compliment later on in later years. He said I was the most apt student that he ever had. You know, it really made me feel good because he had some really fantastic trombone players that studied with him. I felt it was a great honor for him to have…

But, you know, back in those days when I came along, it isn't like today where kids, they learn about tone -- intonation and all this before they even get the instruments they learn. There was no road to go on. We had to make our own road for the kids, you know, today, back there in those days. Really because all a trombone player did back then was -- (imitates a trombone). That's the only way they played. They didn't know any other way to play.
